Warning signs often discussed in prevention research include sudden isolation from prior friends or family, adoption of rigid us-versus-them beliefs, intense fixation on grievance narratives, rapid consumption of violent extremist propaganda, pressure to keep new relationships or online communities secret, glorification of martyrdom or political violence, and abrupt rejection of dissenting information.

Protective factors include strong family and community ties, trusted mentors, media literacy, access to mental health support, opportunities for belonging and purpose outside extremist spaces, and early intervention when a person shows escalating fascination with violence.
